  1. SDxCentral · Oct 23, 2026 · Industry news

    KDDI and Broadcom test co-packaged optics in Japan

    KDDI and Broadcom announced a collaboration testing co-packaged optics (CPO) technology at a KDDI data center using Broadcom's Tomahawk 6 Ethernet switch chip with Davisson optical engines. The testing focuses on GPU-to-GPU communications for AI data centers.

    Why it matters CPO transitions from research prototype to production validation by tier-1 telecom operators, accelerating adoption timelines for power-efficient, high-density AI fabrics in commercial deployments outside hyperscaler-only environments.

    Oct 23, 2026 edition

  2. Financial Content / IP Infusion · Oct 14, 2026 · Vendor release

    IP Infusion OcNOS adds Broadcom Tomahawk 6 at 102.4 terabits

    IP Infusion announced OcNOS-DC support for Broadcom Tomahawk 6, enabling 102.4 Tbps fabric with 512 ports of 200G, supporting scale-up clusters of 128,000 XPUs in a two-layer leaf-spine topology.

    Why it matters Eliminates super-spine layers and reduces hop count, cutting latency and optics cost while maintaining lossless RoCEv2 at full line rate for AI workloads.

    Oct 18, 2026 edition

  3. Business Wire · Oct 14, 2026 · Vendor release

    IP Infusion's OcNOS adds support for Broadcom Tomahawk 6

    IP Infusion announced OcNOS-DC network operating system support for Broadcom Tomahawk 6-based platforms, extending support across 40+ open hardware platforms and doubling bandwidth to 102.4 Tbps for next-generation AI and cloud networks with production-grade RoCEv2, dynamic load balancing, and UEC compliance.

    Why it matters OcNOS-DC on Tomahawk 6 provides production-grade lossless RoCEv2 and UEC support across multiple ODM platforms, reducing operational friction and training burden for hyperscalers deploying next-gen AI fabric at scale.

    Oct 17, 2026 edition

  4. IEEE Comsoc · Oct 13, 2026 · Industry news

    Broadcom demos Tomahawk 6 co-packaged optics at OCP Summit

    At OCP Summit, Broadcom demonstrated 102.4 Tbps single-chip Tomahawk 6 switching capacity and third-generation TH6-Davisson Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) for gigawatt-scale clusters exceeding 100,000 parallel AI accelerators. The open Ethernet fabric eliminates proprietary lock-in while delivering power-efficient switching.

    Why it matters Tomahawk 6 and third-gen CPO are the first production-ready 102.4T Ethernet switches with integrated optics—eliminating pluggable transceiver power budgets and enabling two-tier topologies for 100K+ cluster scale.

    Oct 15, 2026 edition

  5. StorageNewsletter · Oct 15, 2026 · Vendor release

    Celestica ships 102.4T liquid-cooled switch with co-packaged optics

    Celestica introduced the DS6005, a 102.4Tbps fully liquid-cooled data center switch built on Broadcom Tomahawk 6–Davisson with co-packaged optics, delivering 64×1.6T ports in 1.5RU for OCP ORv3 deployments. CPO architecture eliminates traditional front-panel pluggable transceivers.

    Why it matters DS6005 is the first customer-accessible 102.4T CPO switch shipping; it concretely demonstrates CPO power-efficiency gains at scale and removes transceiver DSP bottlenecks from AI fabric optics.

    Oct 15, 2026 edition

  6. Globe Newswire · Oct 12, 2026 · Vendor release

    Micas launches three 102.4T Tomahawk 6P Ethernet switches

    Micas Networks announced three 102.4 Tbps open Ethernet switch platforms built on Broadcom Tomahawk 6P, spanning 800G air-cooled, 1.6T liquid-cooled, and 1.6T co-packaged optics variants, with production scheduled for Q4 2026.

    Why it matters Multiple vendor implementations of open Ethernet platforms eliminate lock-in and provide migration flexibility from 800G to 1.6T for AI cluster operators.

    Oct 14, 2026 edition

  7. Electronics Media · Oct 14, 2026 · Primary source

    Fuji automates SMT placement of Broadcom co-packaged optics switch

    Fuji Corporation successfully demonstrated automated SMT placement of Broadcom's Tomahawk 6 – Davisson co-packaged optics switch using its NXTR pick-and-place machines, marking the first industry demonstration of production-scale manufacturing for CPO switching silicon.

    Why it matters Successful automated assembly of CPO dies removes a critical manufacturing gating factor and signals transition from lab prototypes to volume production timelines.

    Oct 14, 2026 edition

  8. StorageReview · Oct 13, 2026 · Industry news

    Micas plans Tomahawk 6 white-box switches for Q4

    Micas Networks demonstrated three Tomahawk 6-based 102.4T systems at OCP 2026 with production roadmap: 64×800G and 64×1.6T pluggable variants in Q4 2026, and a 1RU co-packaged optics variant in Q1 2027. All support Broadcom and SONiC stacks.

    Why it matters Micas provides the first credible white-box and open-NOS vehicle for Tomahawk 6, enabling practitioners to upgrade 800G clusters without disruptive topology changes while retaining operational agility via SONiC.

    Oct 13, 2026 edition

  9. GlobeNewswire · Oct 12, 2026 · Vendor release

    Micas launches three 102.4T Tomahawk 6 Ethernet switches

    Micas Networks announced three 102.4 Tbps open Ethernet switch platforms built on Broadcom Tomahawk 6, spanning 800G air-cooled, 1.6T liquid-cooled, and 1.6T co-packaged optics variants for AI infrastructure.

    Why it matters Open-platform alternative at OCP Summit 2026 provides hyperscalers choice in scaling 1.6T Ethernet without vendor lock-in, critical for 8K-100K GPU AI clusters.

    Oct 12, 2026 edition

  10. Broadcom · Oct 5, 2026 · Primary source

    Broadcom guide urges consolidating network observability tools for AI

    Modern hybrid networks spanning multi-cloud, SD-WAN, and unowned internet paths require unified observability that consolidates tool sprawl and bridges visibility gaps. The guide emphasizes unified continuous active path testing, device telemetry, and self-adjusting baselines into a single operational view for accelerated root-cause isolation and AI-ready telemetry.

    Why it matters Organizations must consolidate tool sprawl, bridge visibility across unowned cloud and internet paths with active synthetic probes, and build AI-ready telemetry with correlated hop-by-hop evidence to validate automated recommendations before execution.

    Oct 10, 2026 edition
